findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Command injection via subprocess
 * @description Using subprocess with user-controllable input can lead to command injection
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/command-injection
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-078
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  (
    call = API::moduleImport("subprocess").getMember(["call", "run", "Popen", "check_call", "check_output"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember(["system", "popen", "popen2", "popen3", "popen4"]).getACall()
  )
select call, "Subprocess call that may be vulnerable to command injection if input is not properly sanitized."
findings.hypothesis: Command injection through subprocess calls with user-controllable input

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Path traversal vulnerability
 * @description Using unsanitized user input in file paths can allow attackers to access arbitrary files
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/path-traversal
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  (
    call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember("open").getACall() or
    call = API::builtin("open").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember("path").getMember(["join", "exists", "isfile", "isdir"]).getACall()
  )
select call, "File operation that may be vulnerable to path traversal if path is user-controlled."
findings.hypothesis: Check for path traversal vulnerabilities where user-controlled input is used in file operations without proper sanitization

message.text: File operation that may be vulnerable to path traversal if path is user-controlled.
